Now I understand the issue. The bug is in the `updateTask` method in `src/task-manager.ts`. When updating a task, it spreads the existing task and then overwrites fields with the update values, even if those values are `undefined`.

Let me look at the specific buggy code:

```javascript
const updated: Task = {
  ...existing,
  title: updates.title as any,
  description: updates.description as any,
  priority: updates.priority as any,
  status: updates.status as any,
  dueDate: updates.dueDate as any,
  updatedAt: toISOTimestamp(new Date()),
};
```

The problem is that if `updates.title` is `undefined`, then `title: undefined` will overwrite the existing `title` value when spreading.

The fix should use conditional assignments:
```javascript
const updated: Task = {
  ...existing,
  title: updates.title !== undefined ? updates.title : existing.title,
  description: updates.description !== undefined ? updates.description : existing.description,
  priority: updates.priority !== undefined ? updates.priority : existing.priority,
  status: updates.status !== undefined ? updates.status : existing.status,
  dueDate: updates.dueDate !== undefined ? updates.dueDate : existing.dueDate,
  updatedAt: toISOTimestamp(new Date()),
};
```
